headline: World Cup drives record revenue and EBITDA, net income dips
summary_short: Revenue rose 28% y/y to $4.21 billion on a World Cup-driven 78% jump in advertising, while net income attributable to stockholders fell 4% to $691 million even as diluted EPS rose to $1.61 on fewer shares outstanding.
summary_long: Fourth-quarter revenue grew 28% y/y to $4.21B, driven by a 78% surge in advertising from the FIFA World Cup broadcast and Tubi's AVOD growth, plus 5% distribution growth at Cable Network Programming. Adjusted EBITDA (company non-GAAP) rose 27% to $1.195B as revenue growth outpaced higher sports-rights amortization and FOX One launch costs. GAAP net income attributable to stockholders fell 4% to $691M, entirely because the year-ago quarter included a $282M non-operating gain versus just $12M this quarter; adjusted net income actually rose 32% to $765M. Diluted EPS rose to $1.61 on fewer shares. Cash fell to $4.205B (from $5.351B) after $2.0B of buybacks and $287M of dividends; the board raised the semi-annual dividend to $0.29/share.

drivers.explanation: World Cup broadcast drove a 78% jump in advertising revenue plus continued Tubi AVOD growth; Cable Network Programming distribution revenue grew 5% on contractual rate increases, partly offset by net subscriber declines.

The shard's Yahoo-derived EBITDA fell 2.3% y/y, but FOX's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA rose 27% to $1.195B — the measures diverge because Yahoo's calculation does not track the release's own Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation.

Decline reflects a smaller non-operating gain this quarter ($12M) versus the year-ago quarter's $282M gain, not an operating deterioration — adjusted net income, which excludes that item, rose 32% to $765M.
EPS rose despite lower net income because weighted-average shares outstanding fell to 428M from 457M, reflecting the year's $2.0B of share repurchases.
Cash fell to $4.205B from $5.351B, driven by $2.0B of share repurchases and $287M of dividends paid, partially offset by $1.97B of operating cash flow.

CEO Lachlan Murdoch called fiscal 2026 "an exceptional year for FOX" on record World Cup-driven revenue and EBITDA; the company also announced its planned Roku acquisition and the FOX One streaming launch during the year.
